title: RUN to go see Burnout Paradise (no treadmill required) #NYCTheatre #T...
transcript: Okay, stop me if you've heard this one. Four actors on treadmills completing tasks that, let's face it, should not be done on treadmills. And if they don't complete the tasks, they will offer you a refund for your ticket. Which, while it didn't happen at my show, does genuinely happen. That is the, quite frankly, bonkers premise behind the new show, Burnout Paradise. And for my money, it is the most fun show in New York right now. This show is heavy on audience participation. Although if you don't wanna participate, you certainly don't have to. But throughout the show, audience members are constantly asked to come up onto the stage to help the actors out with their tasks. Because like I said, they are on treadmills the entire time they are doing tasks. So they may ask you to hand them a certain prop or to cross a completed task off the list. One audience member actually shaved one of the actors heads, which was crazy. I was invited up to peel some garlic for the cooking station, because, yes, one of the treadmills is cooking a full three course meal, which is served live on stage to two lucky audience members chosen at the top of the show. I don't wanna spoil too many of the tasks because so much of the fun of the show is seeing what wild thing they're gonna do next. But you really do get so invested in the completion of these tasks. And I have now seen the show twice, and it was down to the very last second both times. There is truly no other show quite like this one, so I highly recommend going to check out Burnout Paradise. And every show is different, so it is infinitely rewatchable. And I hope it runs forever. No pun intended.
